claim: Piraeus, Rafina and Lavrio serve different island groups, and each needs a different minimum connection buffer after an international flight.
quote: Direct metro, 15-25 minutes from the centre

claim: Transfer times and costs from Athens airport and central Athens to Piraeus, Rafina and Lavrio, including KTEL terminals and taxi fares.
quote: Metro (Blue Line): ~1 hour, €9 one-way ... Bus X96: 24-hour express, €5.50, ~1.5 hours ... Rafina from City Center: Bus KTEL departs every 45 minutes from Pedion Areos, €3, ~70 minutes

claim: Piraeus assigns departures to numbered gates E1-E9 by destination and vessel, with Cyclades sailings split across E6/E7 and Saronic high-speeds at E9.
quote: BLUE STAR PAROS operates to Syros, Tinos, and Mykonos (E6 passengers only; E7 for passengers and vehicles)

claim: 2026 durations, frequencies and starting fares for the main routes out of Piraeus.
quote: Santorini: starting at €39, with up to 9 daily ferries ... as little as 3 hours 55 minutes. Heraklion (Crete): from €27.50, up to 6 daily ferries taking 7-13 hours. Rhodes: beginning at €46.50, 1-2 daily services requiring 12-22 hours.

claim: Rafina-Mykonos runs up to 10 times daily in summer on Fast Ferries, Golden Star and SeaJets, 2h05-4h40, from €35.50.
quote: Travel time ranges from 2 hr 5 min to over 4 hr 40 min ... up to 10 daily crossings ... Tickets begin at €35.50 per adult passenger.

claim: 2026 Rafina route fares to Andros, Tinos and Mykonos and the operator list serving Piraeus.
quote: Rafina-Andros: Up to 11 daily crossings, ~€25. Rafina-Tinos: Up to 12 daily crossings, ~€30. Rafina-Mykonos: Up to 12 daily crossings, ~€38

claim: High-speed catamarans cost roughly double a conventional car ferry, and SeaJets seats, cabins and car spots sell out in July-August.
quote: a high speed catamaran can cost double the price of a conventional car ferry ... high speed ferries (SeaJets), private cabins, and car spots frequently sell out in July and August

claim: For the July 15-September 15 peak, book 2-3 months ahead, and 3-4 months for August cabins and vehicles.
quote: 3 to 4 months in advance ... cabin vanish first

claim: EU Regulation 1177/2010 entitles you to a refund within seven days or free re-routing when a ferry is cancelled, but weather cancellations exempt the carrier from hotel costs and compensation.
quote: reimbursement of your ticket within seven days, or re-routing to your final destination under comparable conditions at the earliest opportunity, at no extra cost.

claim: The meltemi blows June-September, peaks in July-August at 7-8 Beaufort, hits the Cyclades hardest and affects high-speed ferries more than conventional ones.
quote: strong dry north winds that blow in July and August across the Aegean Sea ... Reach 7-8 on the Beaufort Scale, sometimes exceeding 120 km/h ... High-speed ferries are more affected than standard ferries.

claim: Airport to Piraeus by taxi is metered (€50-58 day) not the €40 flat fare, and you should allow 90 minutes to 2 hours before ferry departure in summer.
quote: Allow at least 90 minutes from when you plan to get in the taxi to your ferry departure time. In July and August, 2 hours is safer.

claim: The X96 express runs 24 hours from the airport arrivals terminal between Exits 4 and 5, every 30-40 minutes, to Piraeus port.
quote: departs from Athens Airport every 30-40 minutes ... Athens Airport Arivals Terminal (between Exit 4 and 5)

claim: KTEL Attikis runs the airport-Rafina bus roughly hourly from Exits 2 and 3, ~30 minutes, €4-5.50 cash on board, first 04:30 and last 23:00.
quote: Price: €4-€5.50 (cash only, paid on board) ... Approximately every 60 minutes ... Arrivals Level, Exits 2 & 3

claim: Paper tickets can be collected at the port office with the reservation code up to one hour before departure.
quote: You can collect your tickets with your reservation code (sent upon confirmation) any day and up to 1 hour before departure from the port office.

claim: Blue Star web check-in opens 48 hours and closes 2 hours before departure and issues a QR e-ticket shown with ID at boarding.
quote: from 48 hours up to 2 hours before your departure ... show the e-ticket along with your ID card or Passport

claim: Taking a rental car on a Greek ferry needs the rental company's permission, island one-way drop-offs are rarely allowed, and renting separately on each island is usually cheaper.
quote: Taking a rental car on a Greek ferry requires permission from the rental company.

claim: Ferry permission must be in writing, costs roughly €30-74, and standard rental insurance may not cover the car while at sea.
quote: Never rely on verbal permission; get it in writing. ... Your standard rental car insurance may not cover you while the car is on a ferry

claim: Piraeus-Santorini is 4h50-5h35 by SeaJets from about €79.70 versus 7h30-8h on Blue Star from about €46.50, while the flight is about 50 minutes.
quote: SeaJets runs high-speed catamarans that make the crossing in about 4 hours 50 minutes to 5 hours 35 minutes, with fares for an economy seat starting from around €79.70. Blue Star Ferries operates conventional ships that take about 7 hr 30 min to 8 hours, from around EUR 46.50.

claim: Aegean's Athens-Santorini one-way fares start at €50, with an August 2026 range of about €50-106.
quote: AEGEAN Flights from Athens to Santorini starting at €50

claim: Sky Express Athens-Santorini one-way fares start at €44, with August 2026 dates from €52 to €99.
quote: August 2026 prices range "From €52" to €99, while September offers fares "From €44"

claim: SeaJets' WorldChampion Jet does Piraeus-Mykonos in about 2.5-3 hours and Piraeus-Santorini in about 5.5 hours at up to 50 knots.
quote: The Piraeus-Mykonos leg usually takes between 2 hours and 30 minutes and 3 hours, while the Athens-Santorini journey may last approximately 5 hours and 30 minutes.

claim: Santorini airport advises 1 hour before a carry-on-only flight and 2+ hours with checked bags, and only about 40 taxis serve the whole island at €30-45 to Fira or Oia.
quote: at least one hour prior to their flight ... two or more hours in advance ... Only about 40 taxis serve the entire island. Fares to Fira/Oia range €30-45

claim: Traveller consensus is that catamarans and hydrofoils provoke far more motion sickness than large conventional ferries, which also have open decks.
quote: Catamaran and hydrofoil ferries (superfast) are more prone to motion sickness on the waves. Standard ferries (fast) are much larger and less so.

claim: The 2026 airport metro fare is €9 one-way / €16 return in a separate zone starting at Doukissis Plakentias; ordinary €1.20 city tickets are not valid on it.
quote: €9.00 one-way or €16.00 return ... standard city tickets are not accepted ... The airport section begins at Doukissis Plakentias station.

claim: Piraeus has 12 gates (E1-E12) and wants 60-90 minutes of buffer; Lavrio serves Kea, Kythnos and seasonal Andros; the 50-minute flight still costs 90+ minutes of airport processing.
quote: 60-90 minutes before departure for Piraeus (the port is huge and finding your specific gate takes time) ... 90+ minutes including security and bag claim
